x: According to the Article 93 of the Constitution, The House of the People chooses two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Therefore, no person, who is not a member of the House, can be chosen Speaker or Deputy Speaker. Under Article 94 clause (c) the Speaker or Deputy Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) passed by a majority of all the then members of the House. s:
Consider the following statements :
I. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution.
II. According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political party immediately.
III. The Speaker of the House of the People may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The provisions regarding vacation, resignation and removal from the offices of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are given in Article 94 of the Indian Constitution. In the second proviso to the same Article, it is clearly stated that when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the Speaker shall not vacate his office on such dissolution, and shall continue in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha. Therefore, Statement I is correct. The Constitution nowhere mentions that a member of the Lok Sabha, upon being elected as Speaker, must compulsorily resign from his political party immediately. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha; such a resolution cannot be moved in the Lok Sabha unless at least 14 days’ notice of the intention to move the resolution has been given. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

s: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha enjoys
o: The right to vote only in case of a tie
The right to vote like other members of the House
Two votes - one in ordinary course and the other in
x: According to Article 100(1) of the Constitution, All questions at any sitting of either House or joint sitting of the Houses shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, excluding the speaker or person acting as chairman or speaker. The Speaker or chairman, or person acting as such, shall not vote in first instance. But shall exercise a casting vote in the case of equality of votes (i.e. a tie) and hence decide the matter. In this case, the Speaker's vote will count. According to an additional provision under Article 96(1), if the Speaker's position is challenged by a motion in the Lok Sabha, they will continue to remain in their position until the motion is disposed of. According to Article 96(2), in such cases, if there is a motion of no confidence against the Speaker, they will not be allowed to vote during the debate on the motion, as their presence will not influence the vote. However, during other matters, the Speaker is entitled to cast their vote in case of a tie. This right is known as the casting vote. The Speaker may also delegate this casting vote to other members of the House.

s: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution provides that the Speaker shall have and exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes?
x: Art 100(1) provides the casting vote of the Speaker in a tie, so the answer is Article 100.

s: Present Chairman of Rajya Sabha is -
x: The Council of States, the Upper House of the Indian Parliament, was constituted in the year 1952. However, the origin of the idea for a Second Chamber can be traced to the “Montague- Chelmsford Reform of 1919”. The Constitution First Amendment Act was enacted in 1951. At that time, the Rajya Sabha did not exist. Article 80 of the Constitution deals with the composition of the Council of States. Clause 1 of this Article provides that the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States and of the Union territories. The present strength, however, is 245 members, of whom 233 are representatives of the States and Union territories and 12 are nominated by the President. Currently, there are 8 members ( 3 from NCT Delhi, 1 from Puducherry and 4 from Jammu and Kashmir) elected to the Rajya Sabha. The first Vice-President, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, is not the only Chairman of the Rajya Sabha who has been in the office for two consecutive terms from 13 May, 1952 to 12 May 1962; Mohammad Hamid Ansari has also been Vice-President/ Chairman of Rajya Sabha for two consecutive terms (2007-2017). Parliamentary Committees *The Parliament is assisted by a number of Committees in the discharge of its duties. s: In case of deadlock between the two houses of Parliament with regard to a bill, who summons the joint sitting?
The maximum GAP between two sessions of parliament can be 6 months, which is calculated between
o: Last sitting of one session to the last sitting of the next session
Six calendar months excluding the months in which the sessions are held
Last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next session
First sitting of two consecutive sessions
x: The six-month maximum gap is counted from the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next session (Art 85(1)), so option 3 is right.

s: Minimum how many times the Parliament has to meet in a year:
x: Article 85(1) imposes a duty upon the President to summon each House of Parliament at such intervals that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. So, the Parliament must meet at least twice a year.

s: Session of Lok Sabha is called for at least-
x: According to Article 85(1), the President shall, from time to time, summon each House of the Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not pass between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. This indicates that the session of Lok Sabha is called for at least two times in a year.

s: What should be the interval between the two consecutive sessions of Parliament?
x: The maximum gap between two sessions is six months (Art 85(1)), so the interval must not exceed six months. It is not fixed freely by the President.

s: There are usually three Parliamentary sessions in India, viz. the Budget session, the Monsoon session and … .
x: By convention the three sessions are Budget, Monsoon and Winter; this is not laid down in the Constitution.

s: The Indian Parliament should meet at least ……… .
x: Since no more than six months may pass between sessions (Art 85(1)), Parliament must meet at least twice a year.

s: The period between the prorogation of Parliament and its reassembly in a new session is termed
x: Recess is the period from prorogation to the start of the next session. Adjournment ends only a sitting, and prorogation ends the session.

s: A sitting of the Parliament can be terminated by adjournment, prorogation or dissolution. In this regard choose the correct answer.
o: Prorogation terminates the session of Parliament
Adjournment sine die means terminating a sitting for an indefinite period
x: Adjournment temporarily suspends a sitting, while adjournment sine die ends the sitting for an indefinite period. Prorogation, ordered by the President, ends a session.

s: After the Presiding officer declares the house adjourned sine die President of India issues a notification for ……… of the session.
x: After the presiding officer adjourns the House sine die, the President prorogues the session, ending it. The sequence is adjournment sine die, then prorogation, then recess.

s: House of Indian Parliament are prorogued by whom?
x: Prorogation under Art 85(2)(a) is ordered by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers, not by the Speaker, Chairman or PM.

s: Who among the following issues a notification for progation of legislative session?
x: Prorogation of a session is done by the President (the Governor in States) under Art 85(2)(a), on the Council of Ministers' advice. The Speaker and Chairman only adjourn sittings.

s: The Secretariat of Parliament of India is –
x: The idea of a separate secretariat for the Parliament of India, independent of the Executive, was mooted as early as January 1926 by the then President of the Central Legislative Assembly, Late Shri Vithalbhai J. Patel. Article 98 of the Constitution specifies that each House of Parliament shall have a separate secretariat, which is independent of the Government.

s: The power to recruit the Secretarial staff of the House of the People is vested in:
o: President aftern consultation with the Speaker of the
x: At the administrative level, the authority to issue appointment orders lies with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whereas the constitutional power to frame rules for this entire structure, under Article 98(3), lies with the President, who makes rules after consultation with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. If viewed purely as “who issues the individual appointment orders”, then under Rule 6 of the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1955, the answer would be “the Speaker of the Lok Sabha”, but this option is not given separately in the choices.

s:
With reference to the post’s in Secretariate of the Parliament, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
(1) Common posts may be created for the Secretariate of each House of Parliament.
(2) The Parliament has right to regulate the service conditions of Secretariate staff of either House of it.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
x: According to the Article 98(1) of the Indian Constitution, Each House of Parliament shall have a separate secretarial staff. Provided that nothing in this clause shall be construed as preventing the creation of posts common to both Houses of Parliament and according to Article 98(2) of the Indian Constitution, Parliament may by law regulate the recruitment and the conditions of service of persons appointed to the secretarial staff of either House of Parliament. So, statements (1) and (2) are both correct. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

s: The Lok Sabha Secretariat comes under the direct supervision of:
x: The Lok Sabha Secretariat works directly under the Speaker's control, independent of the executive. It is not under a ministry or the President.

s: The Lok Sabha Secretariat comes under the direct control of the:
x: The Lok Sabha Secretariat works under the direction and control of the Speaker of the House. The Secretariat has supreme authority over its employees, premises, and assets of the Parliament and exercises this authority through the Secretary (as provided by Article 98 and rules 124 and 124-A).

s: What is the quorum of Lok Sabha in relation to its strength?
x: Quorum is the minimum number of members required to be present in the House before it can transact any business, as provided by Article 100(3). The quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is 1/10th of the total number of members of the House.
